summary: one line, one verdict — the column markers and the fence scanner, answered identically by the renderer (TypeScript) and the indexer (Rust)
why: Both sides call themselves lockstep twins in their doc comments, and until this file nothing checked it. The drift that got here on comments alone: the indexer recognized <!-- /col --> as a marker and the renderer did not, so a line an author can see in their editor was blanked out of their search snippets; and the renderer treated a no-break space, a form feed or a vertical tab as indentation while the indexer did not, so a marker one side hid the other printed. Add a case here when either side learns a spelling.
runners: src/lib/columnLockstep.test.ts — isColumnsOpen / isColumnsDivider / isColumnsClose, fenceOpening, fenceCloses

markers.note: the spaces inside are the author's
a CRLF file's line arrives carrying its return
closes nothing: three markers exist and this is not one of them
a no-break space is not indentation someone typed on purpose
a form feed is not either

markers.line: Write <!-- col --> to split a column.

fences.note: a tilde opener takes any info string, backticks included
a backtick opener's info string may not hold a backtick
three spaces still open a fence
four make an indented code block
a CRLF line's return is not part of the info string

closers.note: a longer run closes a shorter one
a closer carries no info string
trailing space is not an info string
